title: A business unit’s first AI model: an interactive guide | halilneed
name: A business unit’s first AI model
desc: From one task to a pilot you can measure, in four steps: the right first task, scores by slice, the level to start at, shadow and assist mode.
ogDesc: From one task to a pilot you can measure, in four interactive steps.
h1: A business unit’s first AI model
heroP: From one task to a pilot you can measure. For the people who run a process, not for the people who train models.
s1p: Pick a task. The task card fills itself in.
note1: A good first task repeats often, has an output you can check and is cheap to get wrong.
s2h: One score hides the weak cases
s2p: Look at the overall score, then split it into slices.
s2cap: I took my own Turkish personal-data model from 0.740 to 0.882 this way, without training a bigger model.
s3p: Answer three questions and the starting level lights up.
note3: A first pilot almost never needs level 4.
s4p: A pilot runs in two stages. Look at both.
r2: Read the score slice by slice
r4: Write the pass mark down first
ctaH: Next: which model for which process
ctaP: Six kinds of model and four questions that choose between them.

js.shareText: A business unit’s first AI model: pick the right task, read the score slice by slice, start in shadow mode. A 15-minute interactive guide:

tasks.name: Sort emails
tasks.examples: 50 or more labelled emails per category
tasks.metric: Share in the right category, per category
tasks.human: When the model is unsure, a person takes it

tasks.name: Pull fields from invoices
tasks.human: Amounts above a threshold go to a person

tasks.name: Summarise requests
tasks.metric: Checklist: was anything critical left out

tasks.name: Approve credit applications
tasks.human: The decision has to stay with a person

sliceLesson: The overall score looks good. Now split it into slices.
Two slices are weak, but they are small, so the overall score hides them.
Not a bigger model: targeted examples for the weak slices.

levels.name: A ready model and a prompt
A custom model
levels.desc: High volume, a team and a budget

questions: Does the input come in a fixed format? (date, IBAN, product code)
Do you have 100 or more labelled examples?
May the data leave the company?
levelWhy: Write a rule, no model needed.
Start with a ready model and a good prompt.
You have examples and the data must stay in: train a small model.
Try a ready model first; if it falls short, level 3.
Start with a ready model that runs in-house, and collect examples meanwhile.

modes.name: Shadow mode
modes.cap: The model affects no one. For two to four weeks you collect scores, slice by slice.

modes.name: Assist mode
modes.cap: Once the pass mark is met. A person has the last word, and every fix feeds the model.
